title: Continuous Batcher Chaos & Regression Playbook
content:
Purpose:
This is a lightweight playbook for intentionally exercising and regressing the continuous batching scheduler to uncover subtle fairness and tail-latency regressions introduced by recent optimizer patches (deadline-merge, microprobe preemption, kernel scheduling changes). The doc captures experiments, quick repro steps, measurement checklist, and mitigation/runbook suggestions.

Background & Motivation:
- Recent change: adaptive-windowing v2 landed in staging (PR#987). Observed intermittent p99 spikes under skewed arrival patterns.
- Goal: construct repeatable, low-cost micro-experiments that reproduce tail behavior, identify root cause (scheduler policy vs. batching micro-architecture), and provide safe rollback/mitigation steps.

Quick summary of hypotheses to test (ranked):
1) Priority inversion under mixed urgencies: higher-urgency small requests starve older large requests that have accumulated KV-cache dependencies, causing cascading timeouts and p99 spikes.
2) Deadline coalescing bias: the new deadline-merge heuristic batches by deadline buckets that occasionally align to produce large batches at flush boundaries, increasing p99 under bursty arrival.
3) Probe preemption side-effect: microprobe preemption logic can prematurely evict microbatches causing requeue churn and tail amplification.
4) Kernel selection path thrash: quantized vs non-quantized codepaths toggled within a batch cause jitter in per-token cost.

Experiment matrix (variables):
- Arrival patterns: uniform, bursty (Pareto interarrival), microbursts (sub-ms bursts), and bimodal (mix of tiny chat requests + long generation).
- Batch size target: soft_max {4,8,16,32} and hard_max {64,128}.
- Timeout policies: fixed 5ms/10ms/25ms vs adaptive-windowing-v1 vs adaptive-windowing-v2.
- Priority mix: % high-urgency traffic in {0,5,15,30}
- KV-cache enabled: yes/no
- Probe preemption: on/off

Metrics to collect (primary):
- p50/p90/p95/p99 token-latency (end-to-end)
- batch formation time distribution (time from first req to batch dispatch)
- batch size histogram and quantiles
- requeue/retry counts and latencies
- CPU/GPU utilization and per-kernel runqueue times
- number of preemptions per batch

Instrumentation checklist (before a run):
1) Enable tracing: --trace=on, collect traces to perf/trace/<run>/trace.json
2) Start eBPF tail profiler collector on worker nodes (flamegraphs)
3) Enable detailed batch-level logs: logger.setLevel(BATCH=DEBUG)
4) Turn on per-request urgency tag propagation in header for observability

Traffic generator quick repro (locally, small cluster):
- Use bench/arrival-playbook.py with flags:
  --profile=pareto --scale=50 --burst-intensity=0.8 --duration=900 
  --priority-mix=15 --kv-cache=on --policy=adaptive-v2
- For microburst: --profile=microburst --burst-width-ms=2 --burst-rate=10000
- Start 3 workers (g4dn-equivalent) with tracing on and run for 15 minutes to collect stable tail samples.

Observations from initial runs (notes):
- run-2026-02-20: under adaptive-v2 with 15% high-priority, p99 jumped from 420ms -> 1.8s in 3 disjoint windows. Batch histograms show occasional 2–4x spike in average batch size coincident with spike windows.
- eBPF profile indicates a higher fraction of time spent in kernel.select_kv_cache when spikes occur (possible KV-cache contention).
- Logs show requeue events increasing 7x during spike windows; trace shows many tiny batches dispatched followed by a large merged batch.

Quick triage checklist (if you see p99 spike):
- Toggle policy to adaptive-v1: does p99 improve? If yes, suspect deadline-merge bias.
- Disable probe preemption: any change? If disabling reduces requeues, probe preemption logic needs throttling.
- Temporarily set max_batch_size=16 and lower hard_max to reduce merged batch hazard. Watch throughput regression.

Mini-runbook for controlled chaos runs (safe to run in staging):
1) Create staging run label: cb-chaos-$(YYYYMMDD)-<ticket>
2) Baseline: 10m uniform traffic, policy=adaptive-v1, collect traces.
3) Flip policy to adaptive-v2, keep other params steady, run 15m.
4) Inject microburst (2m) with high-priority=15% and measure p99.
5) Revert to baseline after 10m; keep all artifacts. If p99 worsens by >2x, open ENG ticket and roll to adaptive-v1.

Data analysis snippets (useful commands):
- jq '.spans[] | select(.name=="batch_dispatch") | .duration' trace.json | stats
- python tools/batch-analytics.py --input perf/trace/<run>/trace.json --out runs/<run>/report.html
- flamegraph: sudo ./scripts/collect-ebpf.sh <node> <run> && ./flamegraph.pl perf.fold > flame.svg

Example trace excerpt (human-readable):
- t=00:12:33.112 : req A (long) arrives -> sits in queue 23ms -> gets temporarily coalesced into batch with 7 other small requests -> dispatch delayed while deadline bucket waits (observed wait 180ms) -> worker selects quant path -> preemption occurs for two microbatches -> A requeued -> total end-to-end 1.2s

Root-cause indicators to look for:
- Consistent correlation between large merged batch formation and p99 spikes.
- Increase in preemption and requeue metrics aligned with kernel calls touching KV cache.
- Change in batch allocator fairness scores: older requests having their age weight decaying unexpectedly.

Suggested short-term mitigations (safe toggles):
- Lower adaptive-windowing max window by 25% as config; observe p99 impact.
- Cap the number of microbatches that can be preempted per scheduling epoch to 1.
- Short-circuit large merged batches: if batch > X and contains >Y mix of priorities, force flush earlier.

Longer term investigation items:
- Simulate KV-cache contention in bench harness and instrument cache hits/misses at per-batch granularity.
- Explore deadline bucketing alternatives (e.g., jittered flush times) to avoid synchronized merges.
- Add age-preserving slots in the allocator so very-old requests get forced dispatch after threshold T.

Acceptance criteria for changes to adaptive-v2: (gates before promotion to prod)
- No >1.5x regression in p99 under synthetic microburst + 15% priority mix vs adaptive-v1 baseline.
- No increase in requeue rate >30% at steady-state traffic.
- All changes covered with unit tests and integration test harness that runs a predefined chaos script nightly.

Next steps & owners:
- Asha: run full sweep with batch_size targets {8,16,32} this week, attach traces to ENG-2345.
- Miguel: add per-batch KV-cache hit/miss logging in staging workers (PR follow-up).
- Rina: build a replay harness that can deterministically re-generate the microburst schedule.

Open questions / TODOs (brainstorm style):
- Should we add a small randomized jitter to policy flush times to break synchronization? Pros/cons?
- Can we surface a "batch fragility" metric in Console per route that warns when merged batches correlate with regressions?

Notes to self:
- Keep runs short (15–30m) at first to reduce noise from cross-traffic in shared staging.
- Save flamegraphs and trace.json into perf/trace/<run> and attach to ticket.

Appendix: interesting logs/grep hints
- grep "REQUEUE" logs/*.log | tail -n 200
- jq '.events[] | select(.type=="batch") | {time:.ts, size:.size, reasons:.reasons}' trace.json | head

End of playbook.

(Working doc — iterate freely. If you run something destructive tag with cb-chaos and ping #serving-runtime on Slack with run id.)
